title: Automated Microbial Cultivation and Adaptive Evolution using Microbial Microdroplet Culture System (MMC)
protocol: Choose a clean and sterile environment as a dedicated permanent space for MMC.
Install the MMC steadily in the chosen space.
Provide an AC220 V, 50 Hz power supply to the MMC.
Create a dedicated folder on the computer.
Save the MMC.zip file in the created folder.
Create another dedicated folder as the "Installation Directory".
Unzip the MMC.zip and save the files in the new folder.
Connect the syringe needle with an inner diameter of 0.41 mm and outer diameter of 0.71 mm to quick connector A and a reagent bottle.
Autoclave the connected items at 121 °C for 15 min.
Unscrew the cap of the reagent bottle slightly during sterilization.
Use a 0.22 µm polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) filter to filter MMC oil.
Sterilize the microfluidic chip and MMC oil by ultraviolet irradiation for 30 min.
Install the microfluidic chip in the operation chamber.
Connect the quick connector A on the chip to the corresponding port of the MMC according to the position number.
Replenish the MMC oil (to about 80 mL) in the oil bottle before use.
Prepare Luria-Bertani (LB) medium and autoclave at 121°C for 15 min.
Take out the E. coli MG1655 strain from glycerol stock.
Cultivate E. coli MG1655 in a 50 mL shake flask with 10 mL of LB medium in a shaking incubator (200 rpm) at 37 °C for 5-8 h.
Dilute the cultured E. coli MG1655 solution with fresh medium to an OD600 of 0.05-0.1 to obtain an initial bacteria solution.
Initialize the MMC by setting the cultivation temperature as 37 °C and the photoelectric signal value as 0.6.
Turn on the UV lamp (wavelength 254 nm) during initialization.
Inject MMC oil into a sterilized reagent bottle using a 10 mL sterile syringe.
Tilt and rotate the reagent bottle slowly to make the oil fully infiltrate the inner wall.
Inject about 5 mL of initial bacteria solution into the reagent bottle.
Fill the reagent bottle by injecting 5-7 mL of MMC oil again.
Insert the quick connector A of the reagent bottle into its quick connector B to complete the sample injection operation.
Wait for the initialization to end and then turn off the UV lamp (wavelength 254 nm).
Open the door of the operation chamber.
Put the reagent bottle into the metal bath.
Pull out the C2 connector of the chip and the quick connector A of the reagent bottle.
Connect the side tube connector of the reagent bottle to the C2 connector.
Connect the top tube connector to the O2 connector.
Close the door of the operation chamber.
Click on Growth Curve to choose the function of growth curve measurement.
In the parameter setting interface, input the Number as 15.
Turn on the OD detection switch.
Set the Wavelength as 600 nm.
Click on Start to start droplet generation.
Open the door of the operation chamber when a pop-up window appears prompting "Remove the reagent bottle between C2 and O2".
Take out the reagent bottle and connect the C2 and O2 connectors.
Close the door, and click the OK button in the pop-up window.
When the growth curve reaches the stationary phase, click the Data Export button to export OD data.
Select the data save path and export OD value recorded during cultivation in .csv format.
Use mapping software (e.g., EXCEL and Origin 9.0) to plot the growth curve.
Prepare special liquid medium and solid plates for MeSV2.2 according to standard regulations.
Autoclave prepared medium at 121 °C for 15 min.
Cultivate MeSV2.2 on a solid plate (diameter = 90 mm) in a 37 °C incubator for 72 h.
Pick an independent colony and cultivate it in a 50 mL shake flask with 10 mL of special liquid medium at 37 °C and 200 rpm for 72 h.
Dilute the cultured MeSV2.2 solution with medium to an OD600 of 0.1-0.2, ensuring total volume is not less than 10 mL.
Continue cultivating diluted solution in shake flask for 5 h to obtain initial bacterial solution.
Take out two sterilized reagent bottles, one for the initial bacteria solution and the other for the fresh medium.
Inject the initial bacteria solution (5 mL) into the reagent bottle designated for it.
Inject fresh medium (12-15 mL) into the reagent bottle designated for it.
Install the reagent bottles into MMC as explained in step 3.6.
Install the one for the initial bacteria solution between the C2 and O2 connector.
Install the other for the fresh medium between the C4 and O4 connector.
Click on ALE to choose the function of adaptive evolution.
Turn on the OD Detection switch in the parameter setting interface.
Set the Number as 50.
Set the Wavelength as 600 nm.
Set the Concentration as 0%.
Set the Type as Time.
Set the Parameter as 30 h.
Set the Repetitions as 99.
Click on Start to start droplet generation.
Remove the reagent bottle placed between the C2 and O2 connector.
Observe whether the maximum OD values of the droplets during each sub-cultivation period have increased significantly.
If the increase occurs and meets the experiment requirements, click on the Data Export button to export the OD data.
Estimate whether the adaptive evolution meets the experiment requirements by the increase of maximum OD values.
Pay attention to whether the stored fresh medium is exhausted.
If the significant increase has not occurred even after the medium is exhausted, extract the better-growing droplets and carry out a new round of adaptive evolution.
Click on the Screening button to choose the function of droplet extraction.
Choose the Collect option.
Click on the numbers of target droplets.
Click on OK.
Wait for the pop-up window prompt to remove the CF quick connector.
Insert the CF quick connector into the microcentrifuge tube as prompted by the software.
Click OK after inserting the connector.
After 1-2 minutes, insert the CF quick connector back and click on OK.
Repeat steps for collecting each new target droplet until all are collected.
Extract a target droplet using a 2.5 µL pipette.
Drop the extracted droplet onto a 90 mm agarose plate.
Spread the droplet evenly with a triangular glass spreading rod (3 cm side length).
Cultivate on a 37 °C constant temperature incubator for 72 hours.
Pick 3-5 independent colonies and cultivate each in a separate 50 mL shake flask containing 10 mL fresh medium.
Shake the flasks at 200 rpm and 37 °C for 48-72 hours.
Store the bacterial solution in glycerol tubes according to standard regulations.
After experiment completion, click on Stop to halt all operations.
Click Clean to initiate chip and tube cleaning procedures.
